# `silk/build/events`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

What a `silk` command did, as a file of events: [`BuildEvent`](#BuildEvent) and [`BuildEvents`](#BuildEvents).

## When to use
Use this module in a tool that must know what a build or a check really did: whether it
compiled or found the program already built, whether it ran the linker, whether it asked the
network, whether a check server answered. Files and timings cannot tell these apart. Set the
environment variable `SILK_EVENTS` to the path of a file before a `silk` command, and read the
file with [`BuildEvents.read`](#BuildEvents.impl.read) after it.

## Details
With `SILK_EVENTS` set, the compiler appends one MessagePack value to the file for each
[`BuildEvent`](#BuildEvent), in the order things happen, and creates the file when it is not there. Each
value is a `BuildEvent` as `silk.schema.msgpack.SchemaMsgpack` writes it. The file is a plain
sequence of values with nothing between them.

Each event is appended with one write, so the events of several processes that share the file,
such as the members of a workspace built side by side, do not mix inside a value.

## Gotchas
- The compiler never truncates the file. Remove it before a command to see only that command.
- A unit that was already built reports [`BuildEvent.Finished`](#BuildEvent.Finished) with no [`BuildEvent.Phase`](#BuildEvent.Phase)
  before it.
- [`BuildEvents.write`](#BuildEvents.impl.write) and [`BuildEvents.append`](#BuildEvents.impl.append) write on Darwin and on Linux with GNU libc, on
  x86_64 and aarch64. On other targets they write nothing and answer `false`.

## Examples
### Write two events and read them back
```silk
import silk.build.events { BuildEvent, BuildEvents, Work }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.schema.issue { SchemaError }
import silk.text.string { String }

effect fn program() -> i32
  ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut bytes = run BuildEvents.encoded(
    &BuildEvent.Phase { unit: run String.copy("hello"), work: Work.Link },
  )
  let second = run BuildEvents.encoded(
    &BuildEvent.Finished { unit: run String.copy("hello"), passed: true },
  )
  run bytes.append(second.asSlice())
  let events = run BuildEvents.read(bytes.asSlice())
  if events.length() != 2 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let done = run Effect.result(program()) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  return done.unwrapOr(2)
}
```

<a id="BuildEvents.impl.encoded"></a>

### Associated function `encoded`

```silk
pub effect fn encoded(event: &BuildEvent) -> Bytes
    ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

`event` as one MessagePack value, as the file holds it.

#### Errors
- `SchemaError` when MessagePack cannot hold the event: a unit name longer than 4294967295
  bytes.
- `OutOfMemoryError` when the `Allocator` cannot supply the bytes.

<a id="BuildEvents.impl.open"></a>

### Associated function `open`

```silk
pub effect fn open(path: &[u8]) -> i32
```

Opens the file at `path` for [`BuildEvents.write`](#BuildEvents.impl.write), and creates it when it is not there.
Answers its descriptor, or -1 when the file cannot be opened.

#### Details
The descriptor stays open until the process ends, and a program the process starts does not
get it. A process that reports many events opens the file once and keeps the descriptor.

<a id="BuildEvents.impl.write"></a>

### Associated function `write`

```silk
pub effect fn write(descriptor: i32, event: &BuildEvent) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends `event` to the file that [`BuildEvents.open`](#BuildEvents.impl.open) opened as `descriptor`. Answers
whether the event was written. A `descriptor` of -1 writes nothing.

#### Details
The event goes to the file in one write at its end, so events that several processes append
at once stay whole. An event that cannot be written is lost and nothing else happens: a
command must not fail because its report could not be written.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` when the `Allocator` cannot supply the bytes of the event.

<a id="BuildEvents.impl.append"></a>

### Associated function `append`

```silk
pub effect fn append(path: &[u8], event: &BuildEvent) -> bool
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Appends `event` to the file at `path`, which is created when it is not there. Answers
whether the event was written.

#### Details
It opens the file, writes the event in one write at its end and closes the file. A file that
cannot be opened or written loses the event and nothing else happens.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` when the `Allocator` cannot supply the bytes of the event.

<a id="BuildEvents.impl.read"></a>

### Associated function `read`

```silk
pub effect fn read(bytes: &[u8]) -> List<BuildEvent>
    ! SchemaError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Reads every event of `bytes`, the content of the file, in order.

#### Errors
- `SchemaError` when `bytes` is not a sequence of whole MessagePack values, or a value is
  not a `BuildEvent`. A span of its issue is in byte offsets into the value that failed.
- `OutOfMemoryError` when the `Allocator` cannot supply the events.
